inputs.note: MODE: pure data + pure functions. app/supervisor/critical.py's threshold table, checked as data, plus its own lookup and evaluation. No graph, no model.

expected: Every row of the critical-value threshold table states at least one limit, names the units its limits are written in, and is reachable by LOINC code or printed name. Potassium 6.8 mmol/L evaluates critically high, 4.1 does not, and the same number in a unit the row does not declare does not match at all.
guards_against: A threshold table that cannot fire. It is the only thing between a panic value and silence, and every way it fails is quiet: a row with no limit never triggers, a row with no units compares numbers that are not the same quantity (6.8 mmol/L against a mg/dL limit), and a row reachable by neither code nor name is never consulted. None of those raise; they just never escalate.
